title: Returns and Credit Memos on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts
content:
Product comes back only where the programme's returnable classes cover it and only inside the return window, counted in whole calendar days from the delivery date on the ticket it left on, a return offered on the final day of the window still being in time.

**Crop protection.** Crop protection product comes back only unopened and in its original packaging on every programme that requires that, and a part case is not a return.

**Seed.** Seed comes back only up to the seed return cutoff in the season, after which the bag is the member's whether it was opened or not, because the variety cannot be resold once the planting window has passed.

**What is credited.** The words that stood here — *"An accepted return is credited at the price it was invoiced at, not the price of the day, less the programme's restocking charge as a percentage of that invoiced value."* — are **no longer in force** on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts, having been superseded by the current basis on which the credited value is worked out.

**What never comes back.** Liquid fertilizer that has left the plant and bulk blended dry fertilizer are not returnable at all on any programme, because they cannot be brought back into the blend with their identity known.

**Against which invoice.** A credit memo is written against the invoice the product was billed on, so a member returning product billed across two invoices gets two credit memos; a credit memo is never written against the account as a whole.

**A clear account.** Where the account is already clear the credit stands to the member's credit and is applied against their next invoice rather than refunded.

## The window, both sides of it

The clock starts on the delivery date on the ticket the product left on, and the window runs in whole calendar days. The return window, the restocking charge, the classes accepted back and the seed cutoff are each as the member's programme shows them in the plant return schedule. On a hypothetical programme whose window is 21 days, a return offered on the 21st day after the delivery date is in time and a return offered on the 22nd is not. What the window is tested against is the cooperative's own billing record of the delivery — its date, the ticket it left on, the input class of the line and the invoice number.

**The restocking arithmetic.** On an accepted return the restocking charge is the extended amount multiplied by the programme's restocking percentage, rounded to two decimal places, and the amount credited is the extended amount less that charge, likewise rounded to two decimal places.

superseded_clauses: An accepted return is credited at the price it was invoiced at, not the price of the day, less the programme's restocking charge as a percentage of that invoiced value.
